entities.summary: Guillaume de Bray was a French ecclesiastic and Roman Catholic Cardinal, poet, and mathematician who played a significant role in the Catholic Church during the late Middle Ages. Born in the 13th century, de Bray rose through the ranks of the clergy and was appointed as a Cardinal in 1272. He was a prominent figure in the Catholic Church, serving as the Bishop of Münster and the Archbishop of Cologne. De Bray was also known for his poetic and mathematical works, which showcased his intellectual prowess. His literary contributions, including the composition of several hymns and poems, have been preserved in historical records. De Bray's mathematical achievements, including his work on the concept of proportion, have been recognized as significant contributions to the field of mathematics. De Bray's legacy as a Catholic Cardinal and intellectual figure has endured, with his works continuing to be studied by scholars today. Despite his passing in 1282, de Bray's influence on the Catholic Church and intellectual history remains a testament to his enduring legacy.
